chunks: Exalted then be God, the King, the Real. There is no god but He, the Lord of the glorious throne.
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Exalted is God, the King, the Truth' signify in Islamic theology?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often recited as a supplication (dua) to affirm Tawhid and seek refuge in God's absolute sovereignty, particularly emphasizing His title 'Al-Haqq' (The Truth) as the ultimate reality against which all false claims are measured. It connects the concept of divine kingship (Malik) with the Noble Throne (Al-Arsh), symbolizing God's comprehensive authority over the cosmos and His generosity (Al-Karim) towards His creation. This declaration serves as a foundational affirmation of God's unity and majesty in both theological discourse and daily devotional practices.
